description: SAKSHI is a community-operated investigative platform that documents what health AI companies claim versus what independent evidence supports. A project of MIT Critical Data.

title: The Protocol
description: The four-domain SAKSHI investigative protocol: clinical evidence audit, regulatory pathway analysis, financial disclosure map, and patient experience reporting.
cite: The domains and key investigative questions are taken from Table 2 of the paper.

title: Minimum Viable Template
description: A condensed three-domain investigative checklist for community auditors of health AI, fillable in the browser and exportable as Markdown or JSON.
cite: The checklist is the SAKSHI Minimum Viable Template, a condensed working version of the full SAKSHI checklists.

title: Governance
description: How SAKSHI stays independent: design principles, auditor certification, conflict of interest disclosure, the institutional firewall, and the appeals and correction process.

title: Case Study
description: A hypothetical composite case, AfyaScan AI in Uganda, walking through all four domains of the SAKSHI protocol. No real company is depicted.
cite: The composite case appears in Section 5 of the paper.

title: Get Involved
description: Who SAKSHI auditors are, how regional hubs work, the training pipeline, and how to partner with the platform.

title: About
description: SAKSHI’s relationship to MIT Critical Data, its stated limits, the planned evaluation tests, and publications.
